notes.okusinga: Kukira, to surpass: the way to compare.
notes.asinga: Naakira, he or she surpasses (is more).
notes.obuwanvu: Oburaingwa, height: naakira oburaingwa, he’s taller.

guidebook.intro: Compare people and things: bigger, better, the best. Runyankore compares with a verb meaning “to surpass”.

tips.title: Kukira: to surpass
body: There’s no “-er” ending. Instead, say one thing **surpasses** another: **Mukasa naakira Nakato oburaingwa** (Mukasa is taller than Nakato, literally “surpasses Nakato in height”). For things: **Eki nikikira kiri** (this is more than that).
For “the most”, surpass everyone or everything: **naakira bona** (he is the most, of people), **nikikira byona** (it is the most, of things).

tips.title: Same and different
body: **Ni kimwe** means “it’s the same”, and **ni kimwe na** “the same as”. A difference is **enyawukano**. To look alike is **-shushana**: **Naashushana na nyina** (she looks like her mother).

culture.title: Oburungi
body: A common compliment is that someone **naakira bona oburungi**, more beautiful than everyone. Comparisons are a playful part of praise poems too.
